task_text: IKEA MuJoCo STENERIK laptop stand (IKEA STENERIK laptop stand (AA-2372559-2), all 17 operations) with two 7-DoF Franka Panda arms, each with the MuJoCo Menagerie Panda hand (two-finger, tendon-coupled). Build the STENERIK laptop stand: set up the two side supports and the crossbar, drive the six screws through the supports into the crossbar's threaded inserts, then peel the four pads off the backing strip and press them onto the supports' pad sites. Success requirements: Each of the crossbar's six inserts holds a retained screw (its weld to the crossbar latched), aligned to the insert and to the support hole it passes through: axial gap below 0.1 mm, lateral within 0.6 mm, thread axis within 1.5 degrees, slower than 0.02 m/s. Screws, pads and the two supports are interchangeable. Both supports are joined to the crossbar (join weld latched) and at their side pose: gap below 0.1 mm, lateral within 0.6 mm, orientation within 1.5 degrees, slower than 0.02 m/s. Each of the four pad sites holds a pad that is bonded to that support, no longer bonded to the backing, and aligned (same gates). At the end no robot touches any part (the backing strip excepted), every part is slower than 0.025 m/s and the bench carries the parts: on a copy of the state, 2 s with the arms holding their targets, then a 2 N downward load on the crossbar, the bench reaction equals the parts' weight (plus the load) within max(0.05 N, 2 %). The benchmark's terminal rules, the same in every IKEA MuJoCo task, come on top of these requirements. When your rows end: (1) the requirements above hold; (2) the parts are released: no robot link touches any part; (3) every part is at rest: at most 0.01 m/s and 0.05 rad/s; (4) the simulation never broke down: no non-finite state, no MuJoCo BADQACC / BADQPOS / BADQVEL warning, no contact of a part deeper than 10 mm, at any time. The grader then holds your last row for 1.0 s more and requires (1)-(4) again at its end. Mechanism: The M4 x 0.5 right-hand threads are exact convex pieces: a screw advances only by being turned. Retention welds switch on with the measured relative pose once the scene's gates hold: a screw seated in its insert (contact with the crossbar and the support, at least 0.4 turns and some tightening work, held 0.15 s); each support joins the crossbar with the third screw of its side; a pad on its site (0.30 s). The pads start bonded to the backing and come free once pulled off it with at least 1.5 N for 0.25 s.
